_comment: Issue #106 (mobile web v1, the QA-teeth item): combat touch, event-parity proof. Reaches the relc_spar training-yard fight via relc_tutorial.json's own proven preamble (verbatim through combat_started/turn_started{pc} -- PC dex always exceeds both dummies', so PC opens on any seed) then diverges into TAP-ONLY legs pinning the exact keyboard-equivalent event stream for every touch primitive #106 adds: (A) three real adjacent-cell TAPS = the arrow-key move equivalent (combatant_moved/move_pool exact, same tutor beats relc_tutorial's own keyboard route fires). (B) a diagonal-adjacent tap AND a far non-adjacent tap are both silent no-ops (player_cell/combatant_moved count unchanged) -- combat movement has no diagonal and no auto-path-to-far-cell (the plan's 'simplest honest mapping' ruling). (C) an adjacent tap while move_pool is empty is refused exactly like the keyboard case (combat_move_input.json's own proof, mirrored via tap). (D) hotbar_2 arms Dash (keyboard, matching existing mouse-slot-click support), then a TAP ON THE CONFIRM CHIP fires it -- `dashed{move_pool:3}`, byte-identical to relc_tutorial's own Enter-confirm pin. (E) one more adjacent-move tap reaches (6,3), Chebyshev-1 adjacent to BOTH training_dummy_a(7,3) and training_dummy_b(7,4) (skeleton_scene.json's relc_spar roster). (F) opening Attack targeting then tapping a cell that matches NO candidate (a far corner) cancels exactly like Esc -- AP unspent, proven by exact assert. (G) reopening Attack, tapping dummy_b's cell (NOT the default index-0 candidate, dummy_a) re-points the aim, then a TAP ON THE CONFIRM CHIP fires the attack ON DUMMY_B SPECIFICALLY (attack_resolved{target:training_dummy_b}) -- proves the tap genuinely changed the aim, not a coincidental default-target hit (dummy_a would be the default pick with zero tap-select happening at all). Every tap here is `click`/`click_confirm_chip` -- qa/test_driver.gd's `_inject_mouse_click` pipeline (engine-internal push_input, the SAME one mouse_loop.json/combat_move_input.json already use), not a real browser touch event -- the web runner's --touch mode (run separately, see CLAUDE.md's Web QA seeding section) proves the harness stands up a genuine touch-capable Chromium context against this same script with zero regression, not a new per-step touch dispatch tier (that remains future work, see qa/test_driver.gd's own doc comment on the --touch groundwork).
